articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor literally uploaded AWS GovCloud keys to public GitHub because apparently irony is dead and we're all living in a cybersec dark comedy. Nothing says "we protect America's infrastructure" like handing the keys to anyone with an internet connection.

articles.title: The Alert Firehose Finally Meets Its Match
articles.summary: Ghost CMS gets haunted by CVE-2026-26980, a 9.4 CVSS SQL injection that's hijacking 700+ sites for ClickFix scams. When your blogging platform becomes a malware delivery service, maybe it's time to exorcise those demons.

articles.title: Migrating from Go to Rust
articles.summary: TrapDoor supply chain attack poisoned 34 packages across npm, PyPI, and CratesIO with credential-stealing malware. Because why hack one ecosystem when you can ruin everyone's dependency hell simultaneously?

articles.title: The Trump Phone Appears to Have Already Leaked Its Customers’ Personal Information Through a Glaring Exploit
articles.summary: TeamPCP breached GitHub and stole 4,000 private repos using a poisoned VS Code extension, proving that modern software security is basically held together with trust and duct tape. The call is coming from inside the IDE.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Linux Flaws, Defender 0-Days, Router Botnets, and Supply Chain Chaos
articles.summary: Trump Mobile leaked customer data via basic HTTP request exploit because apparently MAGA includes making APIs grossly accessible. The most predictable data breach since someone thought putting classified docs in a bathroom was secure.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a win for end-to-end encryption, reminding us that keeping our digital conversations private shouldn't be revolutionary. In a world of government backdoor demands, actual privacy is becoming punk rock.

articles.title: Akamai Joins Growing Chorus of Vendors Betting Big on Secure Enterprise Browsers
articles.summary: EFF's new guide fights digital surveillance normalization because apparently we need instructions on why omnipresent government spying is bad. Systematic human rights violations shouldn't require a how-to manual for resistance.

articles.title: The sandworm malware strikes: How a hacker group stole 4,000 GitHub repositories and exposed the rot at the core of modern software security
articles.summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing AI discovered 10,000+ software vulnerabilities faster than humans can patch them, creating a digital arms race where the robots find bugs quicker than we can fix our mess. Welcome to asymmetric cybersecurity.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Shifting Identity Security Budget Dynamics
articles.summary: Google API keys stay active for 23 minutes after "deletion" despite claims of immediate removal, because apparently Google's definition of "delete" is more like "delete eventually, maybe." Classic cloud provider gaslighting.

articles.title: mempalace-dashboard added to PyPI
articles.summary: Hookwarden tool promises to find webhook HMAC verification bugs across multiple languages in under five minutes. Finally, a tool that admits most webhook security implementations are fundamentally broken and need immediate intervention.
